summary.what_changed: The docs-agent now detects citations that page-author shortened into an unresolvable form (e.g. dropping a directory prefix) and reports them as an info-only digest line, instead of attempting to repair them. A prior repair capability (scripts/citation_repair.py rewriting the page text) was built, reviewed across four rounds, and withdrawn: each round moved the shortened citation into a region citation_exists does not verify, turning a correct BLOCK into a silent PASS even after the cited file was deleted. Detection now runs via _diagnose_citation_paths in orchestrator_runner.py, after the authoring loop and before the lint-block revert, so it inspects the same finished tree citation_exists checks. Findings are bounded per-page and per-run and classified into four confidence labels (candidate_in_run_inputs, suffix_match_only, ambiguous, no_candidate), with only the first three surfaced in the digest.
summary.why: CCE-141: page-author occasionally shortens an already-resolvable citation, and citation_exists correctly blocks the resulting page every run, so the page is silently never written. An automatic-repair fix was attempted but every adversarial review round (CCE-141 spec) found it moved the citation into an unverified region, producing a BLOCK-to-PASS corruption worse than the original stall. Measurement against the full archived PR history showed zero real firings that a unique-suffix repair would have resolved, and disabling the feature entirely left the test suite unchanged, so the team kept detection-only and dropped the repair/rewrite path.

doc_targets.notes: Describe the _diagnose_citation_paths mechanism, its placement in the orchestrator pipeline (post-authoring, pre lint-block revert), the four confidence labels, and the info_only/bounded-digest behavior.

Record why automatic citation repair was built and withdrawn: four rounds of BLOCK-to-PASS corruption findings, the two measurements (zero real-world firings, green suite with the feature disabled), and the general lesson about not mutating a page the linter already blocked.

summary.what_changed: Fixes a deadlock in the docs-agent nightly orchestrator where the deferral-skip escape hatch (from CCE-140) could never open. The consecutive-deferral counter lives in state.json, which is only updated on merge to main — but the run stays partial and unmerged precisely while the hatch is needed, so the counter never persists and the escape can never arm. The fix introduces a wall-clock-based stall detector: baseline_stall_days reads last_successful_run.completed_at (a durable, external signal unaffected by merge status), and resolve_deferral_stall_days derives a stall window as the deferral threshold plus one, guaranteeing the clock is strictly slower than the counter. When the baseline is older than the stall window, the run forgives the single oldest deferred PR (the cursor 'prefix blocker'), allowing the advance to proceed. The escape is classified info_only and only fires when a prefix blocker actually exists, never on staleness alone.
summary.why: theoju/engineering-docs-agent had published no documentation since 2026-08-22 (PR #240), with every subsequent nightly run reporting partial and leaving the baseline frozen — a 6-night, growing deadlock (CCE-175). Root cause: a counter cannot be a precondition for its own escape hatch when the counter's persistence depends on the very outcome the hatch is meant to unblock. CCE-140 built the escape but never accounted for state.json's merge-gated write path.

doc_targets.notes: Document the deferral-skip stall clock mechanism (baseline_stall_days, resolve_deferral_stall_days, prefix-blocker forgiveness) alongside existing CCE-140 cursor/deferral documentation.

summary.what_changed: Fixes two bugs in the CCE-175 deferral-skip stall clock discovered on its first production run. First, a run that forgives a stalled PR still reported `advance_cursor_backed = False` in the non-truncated (`else`) advance path, so CCE-140's merge gate (`partial and not advance_cursor_backed`) kept skipping the merge even after the escape fired — the flag is now `bool(skipped_numbers)` so a forgiven run is recognized as cursor-backed. Second, the escape was forgiving every deferred PR in the window rather than only the prefix blocker, which meant first-time deferrals on unrelated PRs got abandoned after 0 consecutive deferrals whenever an earlier PR had stalled the baseline — recreating the deadlock the escape exists to break. The fix narrows forgiveness to the single oldest deferred PR (the actual cursor blocker) per stalled run.
summary.why: CCE-175 shipped a wall-clock escape hatch so a permanently blocked PR can't freeze the baseline forever, since the deferral counter that used to gate the escape only persists on merge (and a stalled run never merges). The first live run to exercise that escape (35609168489, 2026-09-21) showed it fired as designed but still could not merge, and a naive full-window forgiveness policy would re-create the exact deadlock by abandoning unrelated first-time deferrals. CCE-178 corrects both defects, verified against that production run.

summary.what_changed: page-author can now cite files that live in a different, declared repository. A host lists neighbouring repos under a new `lint.external_repos` config block; page-author emits a prefixed citation token (`<prefix>/<path>`), and the orchestrator renders that token into a GitHub blob link (for a public neighbour) or a bare basename (for a private one, so the repo is never named) before the linter runs. `citation_exists` never sees the prefixed form and required no change. Undeclared prefixes and ordinary in-repo paths are left untouched and still block as before. The renderer is config-gated: a host with no `external_repos` declared gets a byte-identical, zero-I/O no-op.
summary.why: citation_exists correctly blocks a citation to a path that cannot exist on the host, but post-CCE-140 that block is not a stall: the deferral skip silently abandons the PR and the page is never written (CCE-141's mechanism, hit again in CCE-181 when a nightly on claude-code-self-assessment cited the plugin repo's own CLAUDE.md by its plugin-repo path). The fix avoids widening or weakening citation_exists' existence check (per the CCE-141 lesson: never mutate a page the linter already blocked, since mutation inherits the linter's blind spots) by instead rendering cross-repo tokens into a safe form before the linter runs, plus adding delimiter-guard logic so the rewrite cannot dissolve or corrupt an adjacent markdown code span.

summary.what_changed: Updated CLAUDE.md with three operational learnings from the CCE-181 SDD session, each folded into its existing relevant entry rather than appended as a new section: (1) the SDD pre-flight scan should spend its budget grepping the plan's *references* to existing artifacts (functions, fixtures, signatures, counts) rather than re-reviewing brand-new designs, since all five plan defects surfaced in CCE-181 were stale/incorrect references to things that already existed, while the two tasks inventing new files had zero defects; (2) `prune_merged_branches.py` is blind to a branch still held open by a live worktree, so the worktree must be removed (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) before the pruner can see the ref; (3) a green test-suite exit code does not prove a given test actually ran — `pytest.importorskip` reports a skip as a pass, so verifying a dependency landed requires asserting on a skip-count delta against a baseline rather than trusting the pass/fail bucket.

summary.what_changed: The orchestrator's parsing of subagent output now tolerates raw control characters (such as literal newlines or tabs inside JSON string values). Tolerating control characters removes a stochastic parse gate that fails otherwise-valid runs. An unescaped double quote in a body or title remains a residual, tracked separately as CCE-189.

summary.what_changed: The orchestrator now vendors the plugin directory (passed to the Claude CLI via --plugin-dir) to a location outside the git worktree for page-author dispatches. It no longer uses --permission-mode auto to get past the 'sensitive file' write gate on plugin-dir paths. Page writes therefore no longer depend on a server-side classifier verdict. A new test file, tests/orchestrator/test_plugin_dir_write_denial.py, covers the write-denial scenario.
summary.why: CCE-188 fixed the 100% 'sensitive file' write denials by switching to --permission-mode auto. That mode makes a server-side safety classifier approve each write. On nightly 36241035222 (2026-09-26) the classifier returned no verdict. All ten page-author dispatches failed, zero pages were authored, the baseline stayed frozen at 1718883f, and PR #298 was left open as a partial run. Moving the plugin directory outside the worktree removes the sensitive-file trigger without needing a third party to rule on each write.

doc_targets.notes: Decision record. It covers why --permission-mode auto (CCE-188) was the wrong remedy, and why vendoring --plugin-dir outside the worktree replaces it. Cite CCE-193. The PR title and the squash commit say CCE-192 in error.

summary.what_changed: The fact-checker output schema no longer requires the `ok` field. The orchestrator's fact-checker consumer reads only `verdict` and `findings`, so an answer that omits `ok` is now accepted instead of being recorded as `fact_checker_unavailable`. The change updates `agents/schemas/fact_checker.schema.json` and the canonical schema block in `agents/fact-checker.md` together. It also updates the typed view in `scripts/contracts.py`. It adds tests, including a fixture of the real nightly response that omitted `ok`.
summary.why: On nightly run 36741357748, one of 16 fact-checker dispatches returned a complete answer with `verdict` and `findings` but no `ok`. The schema listed `ok` as required, so the run reported a schema failure and went blind, and auto-merge was skipped as `blind_run`. The orchestrator never reads `ok`. This is the same class as CCE-180 and CCE-125: a schema stricter than its consumer turns a usable answer into a handled failure.

doc_targets.notes: Published contract doc is generated by scripts/contracts_doc.py. Regenerate it, do not hand-edit. It should show `ok` as no longer required.

summary.what_changed: The orchestrator now bounds the source-collector's input window before dispatching it, instead of capping only after the collector has already emitted output. The collector gets a window bound plus metadata anchors, so a baseline far behind no longer produces an output the collector can't fit. The source-collector agent contract was updated to match. Tests cover the window bound and the blind/degraded classification coverage audit.
summary.why: CCE-169's window cap ran after the collector dispatch. With a very wide window (ADIS run 37493982560: 173 in-window PRs, only 12 returned), the collector invented an uncontracted `output_size_limit` error. That error fell into the generic `sources.get("error")` branch and was recorded as blind. A blind run exits non-zero, skips auto-merge and freezes the watermark. The window then widened each night, so every later run failed the same way.

doc_targets.notes: Describe the collector window bound applied at dispatch, before the CCE-169 admission cap, and the metadata anchors.
